scenarios: Real Core, real PTY process and the TypeScript client: a build that prints more than 10 MB streams in order, a client detached and reattached by cursor misses nothing, and older output is read as OutputRef ranges; a long command detached to the background survives a renderer restart and a Core restart (the existing durable handle) and shows the right state; `KillTerminal` ends the process, the transcript records Stopped, and the agent receives one typed event and continues once; user input to a user terminal is journaled and refused for an agent terminal.
proof: Real Core process, real PTY and the TypeScript client; the desktop E2E crashes the real Electron renderer with a background terminal running and shows it reattached. CI run 39873543897 (head df9deca1, PR #111 after main 6e97b019 and #112/#113 merged): all 14 jobs green on macOS, Linux and Windows, including the desktop E2E on all three.
limitations: The CI run is a pull-request run on a head that merged main; no release gate attested; no threshold profile owner-approved. The 'refused for an agent terminal' clause is proven as LEASE_REQUIRED for a client holding no input lease and INPUT_LEASED for the agent while a person holds it (PX-099 semantics), not as a separate user-terminal/agent-terminal split.
